document: cwht preliminary allocation of L1 system requirements to L2 modules and concept elements
author: Claude (requirements engineer role, author invocation); independent review in the L1 requirements record docs/reviews/SRR/checklists/requirements-sys.md (V6); revised 2026-09-25 by the same author for INSP-003 findings 1, 9 and 20
basis: NPR 7123.1D App. G Table G-4 entrance 5.1: requirements ready to baseline and preliminary allocation to the next lower level performed
docs/process/02-requirements-and-traceability.md section 2.3 Flowdown and rule T-18 (SYS_UNALLOCATED: W at SRR, E from PDR)
docs/design/concept.md section 5 (blocks B01 to B22), section 6 (functions F1 to F10 and the allocation matrix), section 7 (module scope)
docs/process/07-software-engineering-plan.md section 3 item 1 (candidate SW-<SUB> module list) and section 14.1 (criticality)

conventions.T-18 reading: A Draft or Active REQ-SYS id is allocated when it appears in requirement_ids of at least one entry of modules[] (02 section 2.3: 'lists the SYS id in requirement_ids under the receiving module') or when its child_ids names an L2 entry. allocations[] is the per-requirement record from which modules[].requirement_ids, elements[].requirement_ids and functions[].requirement_ids are derived; the three derived lists always agree with it.
conventions.modules[]: The six L2 modules of charter section 6 (RX, TX, PWR, CTL, ME, SW), then the candidate SW-<SUB> module files. An L1 requirement allocated to software lists SW (firmware-wide L2, REQ-SW-NNN) in allocations[].modules and names the anticipated SW-<SUB> files in allocations[].sw_modules; the SW-<SUB> entries of modules[] list those ids as the anticipated second-step flowdown (07 section 3 item 1), not as a direct SYS-to-module-file allocation.
conventions.Token mapping: docs/design/concept.md section 7 uses the provisional sub-module tokens SW-SEQ, SW-UI and SW-DSP; this file uses the 07 section 3 item 1 names SW-TXSEQ and SW-DISPLAY (the tokens validate_docs.py and 07 section 14.1 use) and names no SW-DSP file (TS-001 candidate B only; see allocations notes).
conventions.element_ids: Concept blocks B01 to B22 (concept section 5). The architecture ADR at PDR may split or rename them with a mapping table; elements[].code stays empty until design units exist (02 section 7 rows 3 and 4; T-15).
conventions.primary_module: The first entry of modules: the module whose L2 file carries the main child at PDR. Other modules receive a supporting allocation (an interface, a budget share or a sub-function). A system-level budget or environment row (for example REQ-SYS-094, 102, 114, 115, 137, 138, 140, 147) names as primary the module that holds the largest share or the physical boundary, and says in its note that every listed module receives a share. The value 'system' marks a leaf row (tag leaf in the requirement): the main record stays at L1, and modules lists the contributors only (REQ-SYS-122).
conventions.child_ids: Filled from existing L2 files whose parent_id names the SYS id, united with the SYS requirement's own child_ids. Empty while no L2 file exists.
conventions.gaps[]: Non-retired SYS requirements that no L2 module can receive at SRR, each with a proposed disposition; each is a T-18 Warning for the reviewer to confirm or correct in V6.
conventions.excluded[]: Retired SYS requirements, excluded from allocation (02 section 11.3 item 4; T-19).
conventions.change control: Preliminary until PDR; baselined at PDR with the L2 files (SE-42; 02 section 10). Regenerated from the allocation table of the author; hand edits are made to the table and the file regenerated.
conventions.schema: Validated by tools/validate_docs.py against docs/design/allocation.schema.json (the convention of that tool). The schema is proposed by the allocation author (INSP-003 finding-9) and placed by the tools owner; until it exists validate_docs.py reports this file as a failure.

allocations.title: Transmission-length hardware backstop
allocations.note: Proposed at SRR (package decision 38). HZ-004 K12 allocates the second monostable to CTL; it acts on the PA-path enable node of B07 and watches the T/R drive of B03.

allocations.title: Hardware PA over-temperature cut-off
allocations.note: Proposed at SRR (package decision 39). HZ-003 K9 allocates the sensor and comparator to TX; it acts on the PA-path enable node of B07.

allocations.title: Independent frequency verification before and during transmit
allocations.note: Proposed at SRR (package decision 40). The counter must be independent of the SW-SYNTH frequency-word path (HZ-008 K7), so it is allocated to SW-SAFE, not SW-SYNTH; TX supplies the prescaled synthesizer sample, CTL the PIO or timer unit and the RP2350 crystal timebase. The architecture ADR at PDR may create a module of its own.

allocations.title: RF-off level at the antenna port
allocations.note: RF-off level (INSP-003 finding-1): TX holds the main child, the off-state isolation of the PA, exciter, T/R relay and PA-enable path at the carrier frequency; RX shares the level with the receive-mode limit REQ-SYS-176 through the T/R and front-end isolation; SW-TXSEQ and SW-SAFE hold the states in which RF is ended or inhibited.

gaps.title: Build quantity cap
gaps.reason: Programmatic constraint on the production quantity (47 CFR 15.23(a), five or fewer units not marketed), not a property any L2 module can hold. Tagged leaf (INSP-003 finding-20), with a rationale that states why it is verified at system level only; verified by Inspection of the release quantities and the unit serial register. Confirmed by the reviewer in V6; a T-18 Warning at SRR, exempt from the PDR Error by the leaf tag.

gaps.title: Open-source publication
gaps.reason: Programmatic constraint on the licensing of the repository (tagged leaf). No L2 module receives it; verified at system level by Inspection; confirmed by the reviewer in V6 (INSP-003).
